newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat prices steady in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: French wheat prices steady in slow trade.

text.p: French wheat prices were steady on Tuesday in slow trade, with buyers and sellers caught in a war of nerves, dealers said.
Faced with sellers determined to hold on to their prices, buyers were trying to delay purchases, dealers said.
"Nothing is happening. We are just going in circles," one dealer said.
Wheat for March delivery to the northern port of Rouen was bid at 890 francs per tonne and offered at 895 francs, unchanged from Monday.

With little news to drive the market, operators said they would closely watch bids for wheat export licences at the next round of EU grain tenders on Thursday. Bids might provide a firmer picture of export needs between now and the end of the 1996/97 campaign.
"Thursday will be an interesting test (of those needs)," one dealer said.
He said EU wheat export licences granted in previous weeks were mostly to cover old business deals.
Fresh export prospects include a tender Algeria has launched for 75,000 tonnes of optional-origin miling wheat for shipment in April and May.
MATIF fob barge wheat futures for May were bid at 921 francs per tonne and offered at 925, but there was no trade.
